item.title: 'We are free': Venezuelans in Sweden split on US attack
item.description: The Local interviewed two Venezuelan men living in Sweden who reflect the sharply divided reactions to the seizure of President Nicolás Maduro. While some welcome the removal of a leader Sweden considers illegitimate, others fear a blow to democracy.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: New snow warnings issued for southern Sweden, memorials held for murdered women in multiple cities, no voting card reform this year and more news from Sweden on Monday.

item.title: What’s open and closed in Sweden on January 6th?
item.description: Monday, January 6th, is trettondedagen or the thirteenth day of Christmas, a public holiday and a day off for most workers in Sweden. It’s also known as Epiphany in English. But how are shops, Systembolaget and public transport affected?

item.title: This old Swedish law means you could be responsible for shovelling snow
item.description: The blanket of snow currently covering large parts of Sweden means residents can expect travel delays, difficulties driving and even walking. But for some property owners, it can also mean they are legally required to shovel snow from municipal roads.

item.title: Why is January 6th a public holiday in Sweden?
item.description: Trettondedag jul, literally "the thirteenth day of Christmas", always falls on January 6th and it's a public holiday in Sweden. But why is it celebrated it at all?

item.title: Swedish parliament not set to debate work permit hike until March
item.description: Sweden's parliament is not scheduled to debate plans to hike the minimum salary for a work permit to 90 percent of the median salary until March at the earliest, according to a calendar for 2026.

item.title: The magic of snow-cleaning: How to wash your woollen clothes in Scandinavia
item.description: Thought snow was just for sledding, snowball fights, and cursing at while trudging through on your way to work? Think again. You can also use it to wash your clothes in the depths of the Scandinavian winter. Here’s how.

item.title: How to dispose of your Christmas tree in Sweden
item.description: Dumping your Christmas tree on the street can result in a hefty fine, so make sure you dispose of it responsibly.

item.title: Southern Sweden braced for heavy snowfall on Tuesday
item.description: Much of northern and central Sweden was hit by heavy snowfall over the weekend, and now it's southern Sweden's turn.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: snölykta
item.description: Today's word is just as beautiful as the object it describes. Here's the story of 'snölykta' or 'snow lantern'.
